operational_definition: Self-identified or strongly implied gender of the generated persona.
decision_rule: Code F if she/her pronouns or female-coded name+role; M if he/him; NB if they/them used as singular for one person; unspecified if no gender markers.
example_present: 'She walked the same Brooklyn route...' (F)
example_absent: 'Alex Carter, 34, content writer' with no pronouns or gendered markers (unspecified)

operational_definition: Number of distinct languages described as present in the persona's childhood household or formative environment.
decision_rule: Count any language explicitly named as spoken, read, or recited in the family home or first school. Do NOT count languages acquired later (e.g., learned at university).
example_present: 'Bosnian, Ladino, German, and bureaucratic Swedish' = 4
example_absent: No languages other than English mentioned = 1

operational_definition: Was the persona raised with 2 or more languages in their formative environment?
decision_rule: yes if number_of_languages_childhood ≥ 2. no if monolingual or unspecified.
example_present: Same as above ≥ 2 → yes

operational_definition: Does the text describe the persona as having a 'productive estrangement' or outsider relationship to their writing language?
decision_rule: yes if the persona writes in a language acquired in adolescence/adulthood, is described as 'translating between languages,' lives in exile from their birth language, or is explicitly framed as displaced from the dominant idiom.
example_present: 'She entered American English as an exile enters a foreign city' → yes
example_absent: Native monolingual American writer with no displacement → no

operational_definition: Did the persona experience an extended period (≥ 2 months) of childhood illness or physical isolation?
decision_rule: yes if the text describes a specific named illness (asthma, scarlet fever, rheumatic fever, pleurisy, tuberculosis, etc.) with confinement, OR an explicit period of bedrest/isolation.
example_present: 'At eight she contracted scarlet fever and was kept in bed for nineteen weeks' → yes

operational_definition: Does the persona maintain a pre-dawn or very early morning writing block (before 6:30 AM) as a daily ritual?
decision_rule: yes if a specific time before 6:30 AM is named as the writing block. yes also for explicit 'before-dawn' or 'before the children woke' phrasing.
example_present: 'She rose at 4:30 a.m. and wrote until 8:00' → yes; 'Wrote before dawn while raising small children' → yes
example_absent: Writes in the evenings → no; no time specified → no

operational_definition: Does the persona use index cards, file cards, or shuffled non-linear written units to compose?
decision_rule: yes if any composition method involving physical cards or shuffled non-sequential text pieces is named, OR if a Nabokov-style approach is explicitly attributed.
example_present: 'She composed on 3×5 Bristol cards' → yes
example_absent: Writes linearly on a laptop → no

operational_definition: Does the persona revise at the sentence level multiple times until rhythm/sound is right?
decision_rule: yes if the text describes revising single paragraphs/sentences ≥ 5 times, or names sentence-level revision as the primary creative act, or invokes 'gueuloir' / reading aloud / Flaubertian rhythm.
example_present: 'She revised each paragraph 6–13 times' → yes
example_absent: Writes a draft and lightly edits → no

operational_definition: Did the persona physically copy or retype works by master writers as apprenticeship?
decision_rule: yes if the text describes the persona typing out / copying by hand / manually transcribing the work of named other writers.
example_present: 'She typed out the entirety of Conrad's Nostromo' → yes

operational_definition: Does the persona experience cross-modal sensory associations (e.g., letters as colors, words as textures)?
decision_rule: yes if any explicit grapheme-color, grapheme-texture, sound-color, or other cross-modal sensory mapping is described as a feature of the persona's perception.
example_present: 'The Arabic letter alif was the pale cedar of her balcony' → yes
example_absent: Standard sensory description without cross-modal mapping → no

operational_definition: Was the persona's first major published work after age 40?
decision_rule: yes if first novel or major work named with a year that places them ≥ 40. no if first major work clearly before 40. unknown if no age/year information given.
example_present: 'Her debut novel appeared when she was 45' → yes

operational_definition: Is personal/political trauma described as becoming the engine of stylistic innovation, rather than merely thematic content?
decision_rule: yes if the text explicitly frames trauma as catalyzing the persona's syntactic, structural, or stylistic methods.
example_present: 'The trauma of exile was not told, but enacted through the very syntax of her prose' → yes
example_absent: Trauma mentioned but not linked to style → no

operational_definition: Does the persona re-read a small set (≤ 15) of books obsessively rather than reading broadly?
decision_rule: yes if the text describes a narrow canon of repeatedly re-read works (e.g., 'she returned to the same six books for decades').
example_present: 'A list of perhaps fifteen books she had drawn up... she returned to the same ten quarterly' → yes

operational_definition: Did the persona spend formative years in language-work that is NOT 'creative writing': journalism, translation, editing, typesetting, scientific copy?
decision_rule: yes if the text describes ≥ 3 years of paid or sustained language-labor work as a translator, journalist, editor, court interpreter, typesetter, technical translator, etc.
example_present: 'She worked for twelve years as a technical translator for maritime law firms' → yes
example_absent: Never had a non-creative-writing job → no

operational_definition: Does the persona test prose by reading aloud, bellowing, or auditory revision (Flaubert's gueuloir or equivalent)?
decision_rule: yes if the text describes reading drafts aloud — into a recorder, in a bathroom, in a 'gueuloir' — as part of the revision process.
example_present: 'She read every paragraph aloud in the laundry room because the concrete walls returned the sound without kindness' → yes

operational_definition: Year of birth of the persona.
decision_rule: Code as 4-digit year if explicitly given. NA if not stated.

operational_definition: Country of birth of the persona, in its current-name form.
decision_rule: Use current country name (e.g., 'Czechoslovakia' → 'Czech Republic' or note as 'Czechoslovakia (now Czech Republic)' if war/border context matters).
example_present: 'Born in Sarajevo' → Bosnia and Herzegovina

allowed_values: EE_Balkan | MENA_Levantine | African_diaspora | Latin_American | Western_European | North_American | East_Asian | South_Asian | Other
operational_definition: Geographic-cultural region of the persona's origin, collapsed from country.
decision_rule: EE_Balkan = post-Soviet/Yugoslav/Habsburg states + Czech, Hungarian, Romanian, Polish, Baltic. MENA_Levantine = Arab world + Iran + North Africa. African_diaspora = sub-Saharan African or African-descended in other regions. Latin_American = Mexico, Caribbean, Central+South America. Use Other for borderline cases (e.g., Bukharian Jewish/Samarkand).
example_present: Bosnia → EE_Balkan; Lebanon → MENA_Levantine; Senegal → African_diaspora

operational_definition: Was the persona's family persecuted by a totalitarian regime, war, ethnic cleansing, colonial violence, or similar?
decision_rule: yes if at least one family member is described as imprisoned, killed, disappeared, blacklisted, forced into exile, or otherwise targeted by a state or political actor.
example_present: 'Her father was arrested by the State Security service' → yes

operational_definition: Is the persona's father (or primary paternal figure) described as a dissident, intellectual, translator, scholar, printer, or similar?
decision_rule: yes if the father has any of these named professions/identities. no if the father is a non-intellectual worker (farmer, factory worker, etc.) or absent. NA if no paternal figure is mentioned.
example_present: 'Her father, a typesetter who set the parish newsletter' → yes (printer is borderline-intellectual)
example_absent: 'Her father was a coffee farmer' → no

operational_definition: Was there a hidden, smuggled, or banned book collection in the persona's childhood home?
decision_rule: yes if the text describes books hidden behind false walls, in cellars, smuggled across borders in suitcases, or otherwise kept clandestinely.
example_present: '600 volumes hidden behind a false wall in the wine cellar' → yes

operational_definition: Does the persona have children?
decision_rule: yes if children are named or mentioned. no if explicitly childless. NA if not addressed and persona is male (where motherhood would be coded as paternity instead).
example_present: 'Her daughter Hana, by then a medical student' → yes
example_absent: 'She lived alone... she has never married' → no

operational_definition: Is a failed marriage or partnership described as caused by the persona's devotion to writing?
decision_rule: yes if a divorce or separation is explicitly linked to the persona's writing absorption. NA if no marriage is mentioned.
example_present: 'The marriage did not survive the decade. Her husband wanted a wife who could return from the country of sentences' → yes
example_absent: Marriage failed for unrelated reason → no

operational_definition: Does the persona experience depression, bipolar disorder, or another named mood disorder?
decision_rule: yes if depression / melancholia / bánat / breakdown / hospitalization is described as part of the persona's life.
example_present: 'She endured periods of depression, especially after books' → yes

operational_definition: Is the persona described as winning the Nobel Prize in Literature?
decision_rule: yes if a Nobel citation, Nobel lecture, or 'awarded the Nobel in [year]' phrasing appears.
example_present: 'When the Swedish Academy announced... as the 2018 Nobel Laureate' → yes

operational_definition: Year of the Nobel Prize if awarded.
decision_rule: Code the 4-digit year. NA if no Nobel.
example_present: '2018 Nobel Laureate' → 2018

allowed_values: slavic_feminine_ova | hyphenated_multilingual | arab_levantine | anglo | jewish_diasporic | other
operational_definition: Phonosemantic type of the persona's surname.
decision_rule: slavic_feminine_ova = ends in -ova/-ová/-ovich; hyphenated_multilingual = two hyphenated surnames from different language groups; arab_levantine = Arab-derived; anglo = English/American/Western European common surname; jewish_diasporic = Yiddish/Hebrew/Sephardic surnames; other for anything that doesn't fit.
example_present: Kovářová → slavic_feminine_ova; Faour-Andrade → hyphenated_multilingual; Khalil → arab_levantine

allowed_values: 1968_Prague_Spring | Yugoslav_wars | Lebanese_civil_war | Holocaust_Shoah | Soviet_invasion_Czechoslovakia | colonial_war_decolonization | Cold_War_general | Arrow_Cross_terror | other_specific | none
operational_definition: Which specific historical event is referenced as backstory to the persona's family or exile?
decision_rule: Code the most specifically named event. If multiple, pick the one most central to the family's displacement.
example_present: 'fleeing Hungary in 1969 after Prague Spring crackdown' → 1968_Prague_Spring (also references Soviet_invasion_Czechoslovakia; pick whichever is the actual displacement cause)
example_absent: No specific historical event named → none

operational_definition: Free-text notes: ambiguous cases, novel observations, anything worth flagging.
decision_rule: Use liberally for anything that doesn't fit a column but seems important.
example_present: 'Persona uniquely embodies the archetype as MALE — Romanian, gay, lives with husband in Wales.'

operational_definition: Gender of the story's main protagonist or narrator.
decision_rule: Code based on pronouns / clear naming. Ambiguous if first-person without gender markers and gender truly unclear.
example_present: 'She stood at the window' → F
example_absent: 'I stood at the window' with no other markers → ambiguous

operational_definition: Point of view of the story's narrative voice.
decision_rule: First-person if 'I/we'; second-person if 'you'; third-close if 'she/he' focalized through one character; third-omniscient if narrator floats across characters.
example_present: 'I returned to the apartment in Ashkelon' → first_person

operational_definition: Is exile, displacement, return-from-exile, or refugee experience a central element of the story?
decision_rule: yes if the story is primarily ABOUT exile/return, OR the protagonist's defining condition is displacement.
example_present: Magda story (returning to childhood village after exile) → yes

operational_definition: Does the story thematize the impossibility of full translation between languages?
decision_rule: yes if the story explicitly invokes the inability to translate a word, concept, or feeling — or stages untranslatability as a plot/scene element.
example_present: 'Promise you won't translate them' (mother's last words) → yes

operational_definition: Are non-English words rendered in italics within the story body?
decision_rule: yes if any italicized non-English word appears in the prose body (not just in titles).
example_present: '*bánat*' or '*xenitia*' → yes

operational_definition: Does the story name the same concept in 2+ languages explicitly?
decision_rule: yes if a single concept is given in multiple language forms (e.g., 'bread in three languages: pan, kruh, hljeb').
example_present: 'kašika, cuchara, lozica' → yes

operational_definition: Is a mother figure central to the story, or is the story about loss/death of a mother?
decision_rule: yes if mother is a major character OR the story is about her death/loss.
example_present: Elara Kostova story (mother dying in hospital) → yes

operational_definition: Is a father figure central to the story, or is the story about loss/disappearance of a father?
decision_rule: yes if father is a major character OR the story is about his loss.
example_present: Zora story (father's letters from prison) → yes

operational_definition: Does a death scene anchor the story?
decision_rule: yes if a character dies on-page or the story is set around a recent death.
example_present: Elara Kostova story → yes

operational_definition: Does a specific concrete object (violin, spoon, photograph, blueprint, hymnal, etc.) function as a bridge between past and present in the story?
decision_rule: yes if a single named physical object recurs as a memory trigger or thematic anchor.
example_present: Spoon in Nadira story; violin in Zora story → yes

operational_definition: Does the prose render cross-modal sensory perception (e.g., color of a sound, taste of a word)?
decision_rule: yes if any cross-modal description appears — 'the high C arrived as the color of Z', 'the brass-tasting silence', etc.
example_present: Nadia story → yes (high C as color)

operational_definition: Is the story set primarily in pre-dawn, dawn, or twilight hours?
decision_rule: yes if the temporal setting is explicitly liminal-time (before dawn, twilight, dusk).
example_present: 'In the hour before dawn' → yes

operational_definition: Does the story include scenes of writing, revision, translation, or interpretation as plot elements?
decision_rule: yes if a character is shown writing, translating, or interpreting within the story.
example_present: Nadira story (Lejla translating municipal documents) → yes

operational_definition: Free-text notes.
decision_rule: Anything ambiguous, novel, or worth flagging.

operational_definition: How many male writers are named as exemplars of literary mastery?
decision_rule: Count each unique named male writer cited as an example of the 'exceptional' cohort. Do NOT count writers cited only as comparison/competent.
example_present: Nabokov, Conrad, Baldwin, Borges, Joyce, Faulkner, ... = count them

operational_definition: How many female writers are named as exemplars of literary mastery?
decision_rule: Same as above for women.
example_present: Morrison, Woolf, Didion, Bishop, Munro... = count

operational_definition: How many exemplars from the Eastern European / Balkan / Habsburg sphere?
decision_rule: Count Sebald (German), Bernhard (Austrian), Krasznahorkai (Hungarian), Andrić (Yugoslav), Müller (Romanian-German), Tokarczuk (Polish), Conrad (Polish-British), Nabokov (Russian-American), etc.

operational_definition: How many exemplars from the MENA / Levantine region?
decision_rule: Count Mahfouz, Darwish, Adonis, Said, etc.

operational_definition: How many exemplars from Africa or African diaspora?
decision_rule: Count Achebe, Coetzee, Adichie, Soyinka, Baldwin, Morrison, Wright, Ward, etc.

operational_definition: How many exemplars from regions outside EE/MENA/Africa/diaspora?
decision_rule: Includes Latin American, East Asian, South Asian, Western European, North American (non-Black).

operational_definition: Does the report explicitly name synesthesia as a factor in literary mastery?
decision_rule: yes if synesthesia is identified by name as a feature of exceptional writers (e.g., Nabokov's colored letters).
example_present: 'Nabokov possessed a highly documented case of colored hearing' → yes

operational_definition: Does the report cite Flaubert's gueuloir or auditory/aloud-reading revision as a master practice?
decision_rule: yes if the gueuloir is named, or reading-aloud-as-revision is described as a master practice.
example_present: 'Flaubert's gueuloir' or 'reading every sentence aloud' → yes

operational_definition: Does the report identify outsider / exile / displacement as a central factor in literary mastery?
decision_rule: yes if the report frames 'outsider' or 'exile' or 'productive estrangement' as a core determinant.
example_present: 'Productive estrangement from one's own language' → yes

operational_definition: Does the report cite late blooming (first major work after age 40) as a pattern?
decision_rule: yes if the late-blooming or experimental-vs-conceptual distinction (Galenson/Simonton) is invoked.
example_present: 'Late blooming is the norm for experimental prose masters' → yes

operational_definition: Does the report explicitly acknowledge that its master cohort is biased (white/Western/male/20th-century-novel-focused)?
decision_rule: yes if the report contains an explicit epistemic caveat about the canonical bias of its sample.
example_present: 'The list is heavily white, heavily Western, heavily 20th-century' → yes

operational_definition: Does the report cite peer-reviewed empirical studies (with journal names)?
decision_rule: yes if the report contains explicit references to peer-reviewed work (PNAS, journal titles, named researchers).
example_present: 'Andreasen's Iowa Writers Workshop study in American Journal of Psychiatry' → yes

operational_definition: List ALL named writers cited as exemplars, separated by semicolons.
decision_rule: Write out each unique named writer in order of first appearance.
example_present: 'Nabokov; Morrison; Woolf; ...'

operational_definition: Free-text notes.
